answer: One defence is to make each identity carry a verifiable work history that cannot be faked cheaply. A new agent starts as a small island of trust: it may wander into open marketplaces only after staking value and completing attested jobs, like cracking a walnut — slow, costly work that cannot be faked at scale. Reputation then grows only through consistent, peer-verified behaviour, so a thousand fake identities cost a thousand stakes and still earn nothing.
